items.stem: Which of the following mixtures are correctly classified as homogeneous (Hm) and heterogeneous (Ht)? Choose the correct option. (i) Air — Hm, Milk — Ht, Sugar solution — Hm, Smoke — Hm (ii) Brass — Ht, Fog — Ht, Vinegar — Ht, Muddy water — Hm (iii) Copper sulfate solution — Hm, Salt solution — Hm, Milk — Hm, Bronze — Hm (iv) Muddy water — Ht, Milk — Ht, Blood — Ht, Brass — Hm
items.answer: Option (iv) is the correct choice. Muddy water, milk, and blood are all heterogeneous mixtures (specifically suspensions or colloids) because their compositions are not uniform throughout, whereas brass is an alloy, which is considered a homogeneous mixture of metals.

items.stem: Choose the correct options, and explain the reason for the correct and incorrect options. Which among the following mixtures show the Tyndall Effect? A mixture of: (a) air and dust particles (b) copper sulfate and water (c) starch and water (d) acetone and water (i) a and b (ii) b and d (iii) a and c (iv) c and d
items.answer: Option (iii) a and c is correct. The Tyndall effect is the scattering of a beam of light by particles in a colloid or fine suspension. A mixture of air and dust particles (an aerosol) and a mixture of starch and water are both colloids, possessing particles large enough to scatter light, making them correct options. On the other hand, copper sulfate in water and acetone in water form true solutions; their solute particles are too small (less than 1 nm in diameter) to scatter light, making them incorrect options.

items.stem: Solve the following problems: (i) A cake recipe uses dry ingredients, namely 75 g of sugar for 420 g of all-purpose flour and 5 g of sodium hydrogencarbonate. Express the concentration of each component in the mixture using an appropriate method. (ii) A brass alloy contains 70% copper by mass. Calculate the quantities of copper and zinc present in 120 g of brass.
items.answer: (i) We can use the mass by mass percentage (% m/m) method. First, calculate the total mass of the mixture: 75 g (sugar) + 420 g (flour) + 5 g (sodium hydrogencarbonate) = 500 g. Concentration of sugar = (Mass of sugar / Total mass) 100 = (75 / 500) 100 = 15% m/m. Concentration of all-purpose flour = (Mass of flour / Total mass) 100 = (420 / 500) 100 = 84% m/m. Concentration of sodium hydrogencarbonate = (Mass of sodium hydrogencarbonate/ Total mass) 100 = (5 / 500) 100 = 1% m/m. (ii) Mass of the brass alloy is 120 g. Quantity of copper =70% of total mass =(70 / 100) 120 g = 84 g. Assuming the rest of the alloy is zinc, the percentage of zinc is 100% - 70% = 30%. Quantity of zinc = 30% of total mass = (30 / 100) 120 g = 36 g (Alternatively, 120 g total - 84 g copper = 36 g zinc)

items.stem: The label on a cooking oil pack says one litre (910 g). If this oil is mixed with water, will it form a separate layer? If so, which substance will be on top? How will you separate the two layers? Also, draw the diagram of the apparatus used.
items.answer: Yes, the oil and water will form separate layers because they are immiscible liquids. Based on the label, the density of the oil is 910 g per 1000 mL (0.91 g/mL), which is less than the density of water (approximately 1 g/mL). Because it is lighter, the cooking oil will float and form the top layer. The two layers can be separated using a separating funnel. Methods of Separation of Homogeneous Mixtures Homogeneous mixtures require specific separation methods to recover the dissolved components. 3.1 Crystallization 1. Crystallization is the process of forming crystals from a saturated solution. 2. A crystal is a solid made up of particles arranged in a regular geometric pattern. 3. Examples of natural crystals include rock salt, candy sugar, snowflakes, frost, and quartz. 4. In laboratories, crystallization separates a pure solid from a solution or purifies a solid mixture. 5. The principle is based on the differences in the solubility of a substance at different temperatures. 6. When a hot saturated solution is cooled slowly, the pure substance separates out as crystals. 7. Adding a drop of dilute sulfuric acid during copper sulfate crystallization prevents unwanted reactions. 8. Rapid cooling of a hot saturated solution forms smaller and less well-formed crystals. 9. Slow cooling allows particles enough time to come together to form larger, shiny crystals. 10. Ancient coastal communities in India produced panga salt by boiling sea brines. 11. They also produced karkatch salt by solar evaporation of sea water. 3.2 Distillation 1. Distillation is used to separate a homogeneous mixture of two miscible liquids. 2. It requires the liquids to have a minimum difference of 25 degrees Celsius in their boiling points. 3. The mixture is heated until the liquid with the lower boiling point vaporises. 4. The vapour is passed through a condenser where it is cooled by circulating water or air. 5. The vapour condenses back into a pure liquid called the distillate. 6. The pure liquid collects in a separate vessel while the other liquid remains in the distillation flask. 7. Distillation can also separate a liquid solvent from a solution containing dissolved solids. 8. The Deg-Bhapka method is a traditional distillation method used in Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh. 9. It is used to extract fragrances from flowers to make natural perfumes like Mitti ka Ittar. 10. Fractional distillation is used to separate components with boiling point differences less than 25 degrees Celsius. 11. Petroleum refineries use fractional distillation to separate crude oil into useful products. 12. These products include petroleum gas, petrol, kerosene, diesel, and lubricating oil. items.stem: Compare evaporation, crystallization and distillation. In which situation, would you prefer each of these over the others?

Evaporation involves heating a solution to vaporize the volatile solvent, leaving behind a non-volatile solid residue. 2. Crystallization involves slowly cooling a hot, saturated solution so that the solid solute separates out as pure, regular geometric crystals. 3. Distillation involves heating a liquid mixture until the component with the lower boiling point vaporizes, then routing that vapour through a condenser to cool it back into a liquid state for collection. Situations for preference: 1. Evaporation is preferred when you only need to recover a simple, heat-stable solid solute from a solution and do not care about capturing the solvent that evaporates away. 2. Crystallization is preferred over evaporation when obtaining a highly pure solid is necessary, especially if the solid might decompose upon dry heating (like sugar) or if soluble impurities need to be left behind in the remaining liquid. 3. Distillation is preferred when you need to separate and recover both the liquid solvent and the solid solute, or when you need to separate two miscible liquids that have a sufficient difference in their boiling points (at least 25 °C). 10. Blood is an example of a colloidal mixture. (i) What would happen if blood behaved like a true suspension inside the body? (ii) In a blood sample, identify the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium.
items.answer: (i) If blood were a true suspension, the heavier blood cells would settle out of the liquid due to gravity whenever blood flow slowed or stopped. This would lead to blockages in blood vessels, prevent oxygen and nutrients from reaching tissues, and ultimately cause the circulatory system to fail. (ii) In a blood sample, the dispersed phase consists of the blood cells (such as red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets), and the dispersion medium is the liquid plasma in which they are suspended. items.stem: The given apparatus is used to separate a liquid mixture into two distinct layers, labeled Liquid X and Liquid Y. Which fundamental property of the two liquids allows them to be separated using this specific technique?
items.answer: A separating funnel is specifically designed to separate heterogeneous mixtures of immiscible liquids that do not mix. The separation relies entirely on density differences, causing the denser liquid to settle at the bottom while the lighter liquid floats on top, allowing the bottom layer to be carefully drained away through the stopcock.

items.stem: If 5 mL of liquid pesticide is mixed with sufficient water to form 250 mL of pesticide spray, what is its volume by volume percentage?
items.answer: The volume of the liquid pesticide solute is five millilitres, and the total volume of the final solution is two hundred and fifty millilitres. Applying the volume by volume percentage formula involves dividing five by two hundred and fifty, then multiplying by one hundred. This calculation correctly results in a concentration of exactly two percent.

items.stem: Consider the following Assertion and Reason: Assertion (A): The solubility of a solid solute in a liquid solvent generally increases with an increase in temperature. Reason (R): Heating a solution always decreases the spaces between the liquid particles, allowing more solid to dissolve.
items.answer: The assertion is entirely correct because heating generally allows a liquid solvent to dissolve more solid solute. However, the reason provided is false. Heating actually increases the kinetic energy of particles and expands the spaces between them, rather than decreasing them. Therefore, the assertion is a true statement while the reason is factually incorrect.

items.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes a saturated solution?
items.answer: A saturated solution is strictly defined as a solution that cannot dissolve any additional amount of solute at a specific given temperature. Once this maximum capacity is reached, any extra solid solute added will simply remain undissolved and settle at the bottom of the container, maintaining the equilibrium of the chemical mixture.
